newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks edge lower ahead of key inflation data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks edge lower ahead of key inflation data.

text.p: U.S. blue chips ended slighly lower on Thursday, posting their fourth consecutive losing session after investors held off bets ahead of key economic data.

On Friday the government will report the September producer price index as well as September retail sales. The data could give the market a scare if they show signs of increasing inflationary pressure, analysts said.
The Dow industrials ended off about nine points at 5922, with losing issues edging gainers by a six to five ratio.
Friday's data are expected to give financial markets an indication of whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will soon have to hike interest rates in order to cool inflation.
"Friday's session is likely to show a reaction to the Fed's interest-rate perspective," said Alan Ackerman, senior market strategist at Fahnestock and Co.
The Standard & Poor's 500 ended off about two points at 695 while the Nasdaq composite eased a point to 1237.
Economists polled in a Reuters survey said they expect the overall PPI to be up 0.3 percent and retail sales are expected to be up 0.2 percent.

Adding to the market's overall indecision is the flood of third quarter earnings reports due to begin in earnest next week, with companies including Johnson and Johnson, Coca-Cola Co, Citicorp and Time Warner Inc due to post their results.
Wall Street bears, a dwindling breed, are saying that the Dow's inability to close above the 6000 barrier is a sign that stocks are losing momentum.
Overvalued stocks, shrinking profit margins and slowing earnings growth are factors that could be leading to a broad market pullback, said James Solloway, director of Research at Argus Research Corp.
"Earnings could be a critical factor here in pushing the market over," Solloway said.
But bulls said they see no major danger on the horizon.

"We don't see much in the way of downside here at all," said Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities. Among factors he cited was "major bottom" established on the 30-year Treasury bond. The long bond was off 22/32 in late trading with its yield at 6.89 percent.
Tower attributed this week's stock weakness to the psychological barrier of the Dow's 6,000 level and profit taking after the Nasdaq composite hit a new high on Monday.
"I suspect it's a combination of those things and working off a little excess enthusiasm here in the near term," he said.
Large chain stores posted mixed September sales Thursday, hurt by warmer than expected summer heat and an accounting shift that left most of the Labor Day weekend out of September results this year.
Sears Roebuck rose 1/2 to 48-1/4, J.C. Penney Co gained 1-3/8 to 53-7/8, while specialty retailer Limited Inc, ended flat at 19.
Among individual stocks, corporate jetmaker Gulfstream Aerospace Corp, which led the NYSE most actives, rose 1-3/4 to 25-3/4 in its Wall Street debut.
Trusted Information rose 4-1/4 to 17-1/4 in its first day of trading.

Eyeware shares tumbled after Sunglass Hut International warned of a third-quarter earnings shortfall. Sunglass Hut lost 4-5/16 to 9-3/16, Oakley Inc shed 7-5/8 to 37-1/2, and Gargoyles Inc tumbled four to 15-3/4.
Olin Corp surged 4-3/8 to 88-1/2 after announcing a broad corprate restructuring, a share buyback and a stock split.

AMR Corp, parent of American Airlines, rose 2-3/4 to 85-3/8 after its chief executive forecast a "decent" fourth quarter and said bookings were "solid." Other airline stocks also firmed, with Delta Air Lines up one to 69-3/4, USAir inched up 3/8 to 15-3/4 and UAL Corp added 1-5/8 to 45-1/8.
Altera Corp rallied 6-1/8 to 60 after posting strong quarterly results. Merrill Lynch, Bear Stearns, Hambrecht & Quist and Robertson Stephens upgraded the stock.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.01 to 1236.97.
The S&P 500 index fell 2.13 to 694.61.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
